endorsements.quote: Researchers should articulate the type and rationale behind their chosen phenotyping algorithms, elucidating why and how different factors were selected in their development, including the intended use.
Consistently reported performance metrics are essential for evaluating phenotyping algorithms.
In addition, phenotyping algorithms must be scrutinized for fairness to avoid disproportionately affecting historically marginalized or underrepresented populations.

unlisted_practices: Researchers should report phenotyping algorithm performance metrics (gold standard, positive predictive value, sensitivity, AUROC, and fairness metrics) consistently.
Developers should use multi-site datasets or techniques such as federated learning to improve algorithm performance and usability.
Investigators should use a common data model such as OMOP when applicable, and provide code based on standard programming languages and common data models.
Investigators should use commonly available programming packages or NLP pipelines and report sufficient implementation details in supporting documents.
Researchers should implement, deposit, and share phenotyping algorithms in cloud computing environments to benefit a broader audience.
Developers should assign each phenotyping algorithm a version with dates validated, modified (including details), and published.
Developers should incorporate a systematic approach to algorithm modification including regular evaluation, updating, and rigorous testing.
Investigators should provide recommended re-evaluation windows or an automatic system to track factors that change algorithm reliability.
Researchers should report the type, use, and training sets of high-throughput phenotyping methods when describing an algorithm.
Researchers should quantify phenotyping algorithm complexity using an index score of content indicators (term counts, operations, temporal restrictions) and technical sophistication indicators.
Phenotyping algorithms should adhere to FAIR (findability, accessibility, interoperability, reusability) principles.

screen.reason: This is a framework/recommendations paper proposing five fundamental reporting dimensions (complexity, performance, efficiency, implementability, maintenance) for phenotyping algorithms in biomedical research.
